name: Carrageenan
aliases: E407, E407a, INS 407, INS 407a, carrageenan, processed eucheuma seaweed, Irish moss gelose, eucheuman, furcellaran, carragenano, carraghenane
what_is: Carrageenan (INS 407 / E407) comes from red seaweed and is used to thicken, gel and stabilise foods. Processed Eucheuma seaweed (INS 407a / E407a) is a closely related form used for the same texture functions.
why_botia: Carrageenan comes from red seaweed and is used to thicken and gel — it is found in plant-based drinks, cream and processed meat. On the label it may appear as E407 or E407a, which is the same seaweed with different processing.
can_1: Detect E407, E407a, INS 407, INS 407a, carrageenan and processed Eucheuma seaweed when explicitly declared.
can_2: Explain the difference between food-grade carrageenan and its broken-down form, and why the smaller pieces remain an open question.
cannot_1: Determine from the ingredient list how much shorter broken-down material is present in a particular carrageenan preparation.
cannot_2: Determine whether additional breakdown occurred during processing or digestion, or predict an individual's intestinal response.

title: Carrageenan
description: Carrageenan is a red-seaweed thickener used in plant milks, cream and processed meat; the unresolved question is how much smaller broken-down material may be present or form.
